quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a surface with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels in a straight line, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: A person's BAC depends on their body weight, how much alcohol they consume, and how quickly they consume it. How often someone drinks does not affect their BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so wind can catch the fabric.
Fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.
Fit tightly so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly enough to stop flapping in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly and maneuver if someone else makes a mistake. Space around your motorcycle does not help you speed up in a curve.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not recommended.
Recommended only for long rides.
Recommended for every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Recommended for every ride.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even when wearing a helmet. Use hearing protection every time you ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, the best way to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on, including your high beam when legal and safe. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Cross into another lane of traffic.
Get through the turn faster.
Keep control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A working clutch should feel:

options.text: Loose and rough.
Tight and smooth.
Loose and smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and smooth.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when you release it, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to cross before a train.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as during the day.
Ride more slowly than during the day.
Ride faster than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride more slowly at night than during the day, especially on unfamiliar roads. Slower speeds give you more time to avoid hazards when visibility is poor.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light will change to red soon.
The light will change to green soon.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will change to red soon.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up.
The same time to stop and speed up.
More time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows a motorcycle's acceleration and braking. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly with a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically by learning your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles link the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn how your motorcycle's braking system works.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT strongly affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
The amount of alcohol you drink
Your body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: BAC is mainly affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Get off the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In the rain, ride in the tire tracks of cars ahead of you, not the center of the lane. The left track usually works best, but adjust based on traffic.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift to higher gears.
Need to shift to lower gears.
Need to put it in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift to higher gears.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, shift into higher gears.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergencies.
Should be used together with the rear brake.
Is unsafe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black symbols alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What is usually the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Leave the road.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make the danger worse because they may tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: How can you be more easily seen at an intersection?

options.text: Keep your headlight on.
Wear dark clothing.
Wave your arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight all day long helps other drivers see you at intersections.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required equipment for a motorcycle?

options.text: At least one rearview mirror.
A horn.
A yellow stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow stop light.
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, motorcycles must have: a seat for the rider; a seat and footrests for passengers; at least one muffler; at least one rear reflector; at least one rearview mirror; a horn; brakes; one or two headlights; a white license plate light; a red taillight; and a red stop light. A yellow stop light is not required.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?

options.text: It helps in most situations.
It improves steering.
It causes control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again quickly. If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Why does a motorcycle rider have an advantage over a car driver when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: A motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
A motorcycle rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
Motorcycles can stop faster than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, you can ride in the left part of your lane. This lets you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only use the left part of the lane if no traffic is coming toward you.
